question: According to the unit, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the background information section of a lesson plan?
options: To list the grammar structures the teacher plans to introduce during the session
To record contextual facts that shape every subsequent decision, from text complexity to time allocated for pair work
To summarize the results of a needs analysis conducted at the start of the academic year
To provide a brief biography of the teacher for administrative records
answer: To record contextual facts that shape every subsequent decision, from text complexity to time allocated for pair work

question: In the Eastern College lesson plan example, why is the topic of road safety described as relevant to the specific group of learners rather than an arbitrary choice?
options: Because road safety is a required topic in all intermediate-level English courses
Because the teacher personally witnessed a traffic accident before designing the lesson
Because most learners hold or are seeking jobs in service industries or technical fields where road safety is directly encountered
Because the course textbook chapter on road safety happened to fall on that week in the syllabus
answer: Because most learners hold or are seeking jobs in service industries or technical fields where road safety is directly encountered
anchor: most learners hold or are seeking jobs in service industries such as retail and hospitality, or in technical fields such as cable repair and mechanics

question: What specific function does the Pre-class Preparation field serve that is DISTINCT from the procedure column of the lesson plan?
options: It records the teacher's reflections on student performance after the lesson ends
It lists tasks the teacher must complete before students arrive, such as printing materials or setting up equipment
It documents the pedagogical rationale for each activity in the lesson sequence
It states the measurable outcomes students are expected to achieve by the end of the session
answer: It lists tasks the teacher must complete before students arrive, such as printing materials or setting up equipment
anchor: The Pre-class Preparation field lists tasks the teacher must complete before students arrive

question: The unit explains that a completed lesson plan serves two distinct purposes depending on WHEN it is used. What are those two purposes, and at what point in relation to the lesson does each one apply?
answer: Before the lesson, the completed plan functions as a preparation guide, helping the teacher think through each stage, anticipate student needs, and gather materials in advance. After the lesson, it becomes a record of what was planned, which the teacher can compare against what actually occurred in the classroom.
anchor: Before the lesson, it functions as a preparation guide…After the lesson, the completed document becomes a record of what was planned
